selection: Seven previously open, nonprovisional catalog entries without prior linked repository results; paired questions share source definitions and reusable proof work.
evidence: Written proofs with separate internal AI reviews, exact finite computational controls, and supplementary high-precision numerical checks. No external peer review, formal proof certification, or exhaustive novelty claim.

results.title: Leontief donation dynamics beyond bounded waiting
results.theorem: For arbitrary positive Leontief weights, convergence holds whenever the consecutive complete-interval lengths L_k satisfy sum_k 1/L_k = infinity. For support weights v_ix = a_i w_x, every fair schedule has finite total variation and converges; this includes every incidence forest.
results.remaining_gap: Arbitrary fair schedules with unrestricted positive weights on incidence cycles remain unresolved.
results.source_access: Original thesis and revised paper read; bounded 2026 literature comparison recorded in the proof note.
results.source_location: Open Problem 5, p. 99 (PDF p. 115); redistribution dynamics and Theorem 5.24, pp. 65–67. Status evidence, checked 5 October 2026: The October 2025 revision of Coordinating Charitable Donations with Leontief Preferences still imposes the bounded-waiting K assumption in Theorem 3. The following discussion removes it only for binary Leontief utilities. Searches through the check date found no general resolution.

results.title: Exact characterization of proper-total-dominating caterpillars
results.theorem: A 16-state weighted automaton characterizes exactly the caterpillars admitting a proper total dominating set and computes a minimum witness. At most three selected leaves per spine vertex and four selected neighbors per spine vertex suffice; both bounds are sharp. The minimum-witness algorithm uses O(k) arithmetic operations for a k-vertex spine; input bit costs are separate.
results.remaining_gap: No mathematical gap identified at the stated algorithmic characterization scope; external peer review and historical priority are not certified.
results.source_access: Thesis full text blocked. Author-written publisher-indexed question text and the author conference abstract were checked; access limits and the related 2026 general-graph paper are recorded.

results.title: Bounds and finite representatives for tree domination pairs
results.resolution: Proved bounds, finite reduction, and two complete slices
results.theorem: Every realizable tree pair (a,b) = (gamma_t,gamma_pt) satisfies a+1 <= b <= 6a-4 and has a representative on at most 6a-4 vertices. The complete a=2 slice is b in {3,5}; the complete a=3 slice is b in {6,7}.
results.remaining_gap: A general characterization of the realizable pairs for a >= 4 remains unresolved; no sharpness claim is made for the upper bound.
results.source_access: Thesis full text blocked. Publisher-indexed primary question text, author abstract, and related general-graph results were checked; known small constructions are distinguished from this proof.

results.title: Odd-cycle obstructions for completely regular semigroups
results.resolution: Proved subclass exclusion and necessary conditions
results.theorem: Every triangle-free commuting graph of a finite band is bipartite. In any finite completely regular semigroup with triangle-free commuting graph, the noncentral idempotents induce a bipartite graph, and every odd cycle contains at least two nonidempotent involutions whose subgroup identities are central.
results.remaining_gap: Odd girths at least five for general finite completely regular semigroups remain unresolved.
results.source_access: Full original paper, exact Problem 7.3, definitions, structural results, and relevant earlier constructions checked.

results.title: No knit degree three in finite completely regular semigroups
results.resolution: Proposed complete negative existence answer by nonexistence theorem
results.theorem: Every length-three left path in a finite completely regular semigroup constructively yields a length-two left path. Consequently no finite completely regular semigroup has knit degree three.
results.remaining_gap: No mathematical gap identified in the written proof and separate internal review. This is a nonexistence theorem, not a counterexample construction; it does not apply to arbitrary semigroups.
results.source_access: Full original paper, exact Problem 7.4, endpoint conditions, and relevant earlier left-path results checked.

results.title: Finite large-parameter Pareto-record dispersion limit
results.resolution: Proposed complete affirmative answer with an integral formula
results.theorem: For every fixed integer d >= 2, B_d(a) has a finite limit C_d > 1 as a tends to infinity. A convergent positive double-integral formula gives C_2 = 1 + pi^2/3 and C_3 = 1 + 12 zeta(3). The n-to-infinity limit defining B_d is taken first.
results.remaining_gap: No mathematical gap identified relative to the fixed-parameter formula in Sun, Theorem 4.8 and Remark 4.10. The proof concerns record arrivals R_n, not remaining records r_n; external peer review is still needed.
results.source_access: Original dissertation downloaded and read; printed pp.72-73 and 263 independently inspected, including visual verification of the rising-factorial normalization.

results.title: Small-parameter Pareto-record dispersion limit and first correction
results.resolution: Proposed complete affirmative answer with a first-order expansion
results.theorem: For every fixed integer d >= 2, B_d(a) = 1 - 2a/(d-1) + O_d(a^2) as a decreases to zero. In particular its limit is one, with underdispersion for all sufficiently small positive a. The n-to-infinity limit defining B_d is taken first.
results.remaining_gap: No mathematical gap identified relative to the fixed-parameter formula in Sun, Theorem 4.8 and Remark 4.10. The proof concerns record arrivals R_n, not remaining records r_n; external peer review is still needed.
results.source_access: Original dissertation downloaded and read; printed pp.72-73 and 263 independently inspected, including visual verification of the rising-factorial normalization.
